personaggioMisterioso.title: Mystery Character Tutorial
personaggioMisterioso.subtitle: Learn how to use the Mystery Character guessing game

welcome.title: Welcome to Mystery Character!
welcome.content: An interactive guessing game where you discover historical figures through strategic questioning.
welcome.bullet1: Interactive educational game for all ages

howItWorks.title: How It Works
howItWorks.content: Learn the basic game mechanics and how to use strategic questions to identify characters.
howItWorks.bullet1: Choose a historical character from Wikipedia
howItWorks.bullet2: Ask yes/no questions to narrow down possibilities
howItWorks.bullet3: Use strategic thinking to identify the character
howItWorks.bullet4: Learn fascinating historical facts along the way

selectCharacter.title: Character Selection
selectCharacter.content: Discover how to choose and configure historical characters for your game.
selectCharacter.bullet1: Access to thousands of historical characters
selectCharacter.bullet2: Filter by era, profession, or nationality

askQuestions.title: Strategic Questioning
askQuestions.content: Learn the art of asking effective questions to quickly identify the mystery character.
askQuestions.bullet1: Start with broad questions to narrow the field
askQuestions.bullet2: Use specific questions for precise details

technology.title: AI Technology
technology.content: Discover the advanced technology that powers the game and enables realistic responses.
technology.bullet1: Powered by advanced Large Language Models (LLMs)

classroomUse.title: Classroom Use
classroomUse.content: Discover how to integrate the game into educational activities to maximize learning.

examples.title: Practical Examples
examples.content: Explore concrete examples of how to use the game in different subjects and educational contexts.
examples.bullet4: Social Studies: Activists, politicians, cultural icons

howItWorks.bullet1: Choose a topic you're passionate about
howItWorks.bullet3: Engage in structured debate with an AI opponent
howItWorks.bullet4: Develop and refine your argumentation skills

debatePreparation.title: Debate Preparation
debatePreparation.content: Learn essential strategies for preparing compelling arguments and anticipating counterarguments.
debatePreparation.bullet1: Conduct thorough research on the topic

collaborativeLearning.title: Collaborative Learning
collaborativeLearning.content: Discover how peer learning and teacher guidance enhance your debate skills.
collaborativeLearning.bullet2: Receive constructive feedback from peers and teachers
collaborativeLearning.bullet4: Learn by observing peer debate techniques

visibleThinking.title: Visible Thinking

visibleThinking.bullet2: Explain the reasoning behind each argument

teacherEvaluation.title: Teacher Evaluation

teacherEvaluation.bullet2: Feedback on argument logic and structure

selfReflection.title: Self-Reflection
selfReflection.content: Learn to critically reflect on your debate performance for continuous improvement.
selfReflection.bullet1: Analyze strengths and areas for improvement
selfReflection.bullet2: Reflect on the effectiveness of strategies used

examples.title: Practical Examples
examples.content: Explore concrete examples of debate topics and effective techniques across different subjects.
examples.bullet1: Ethical debates: Artificial intelligence and privacy
examples.bullet2: Environmental issues: Climate change and sustainability
examples.bullet4: Technology: Social media and societal impact

youModerate.title: You Moderate Tutorial
youModerate.subtitle: Master collaborative debate moderation and critical thinking through AI-powered Wikipedia character debates

welcome.title: Welcome to You Moderate!
welcome.content: Step into the role of a collaborative debate moderator, facilitating discussions between AI-powered Wikipedia characters while developing critical thinking and moderation skills.
welcome.bullet2: Develop critical thinking and moderation skills
welcome.bullet3: Explore different perspectives through structured debates

moderatorRole.title: Collaborative Moderation Role
moderatorRole.content: Step into the role of a collaborative debate moderator, working with teachers and peers to create engaging learning experiences.
moderatorRole.bullet1: Work with teachers/peers to select stimulating debate topics
moderatorRole.bullet2: Facilitate structured discussions between contrasting AI characters
moderatorRole.bullet3: Guide conversations toward deeper analytical thinking
moderatorRole.bullet4: Practice real-time moderation and questioning techniques

peerCollaboration.title: Peer Learning & Teacher Guidance
peerCollaboration.content: Collaborate with your learning community to enhance moderation skills and build confidence through shared experiences.
peerCollaboration.bullet1: Collaborate with classmates in selecting debate scenarios
peerCollaboration.bullet2: Receive real-time guidance from teachers during moderation
peerCollaboration.bullet3: Learn from observing peer moderation techniques
peerCollaboration.bullet4: Share insights and strategies with learning community

setupDebate.title: Strategic Debate Setup
setupDebate.content: Learn to design compelling debate scenarios that promote deep thinking and meaningful dialogue between AI characters.
setupDebate.bullet1: Choose contrasting Wikipedia characters with opposing viewpoints
setupDebate.bullet2: Design thought-provoking questions that reveal different perspectives
setupDebate.bullet3: Create scenarios that encourage deep analytical thinking
setupDebate.bullet4: Balance character personalities for engaging discussions

moderationSkills.title: Advanced Moderation Skills
moderationSkills.content: Develop sophisticated facilitation techniques to guide meaningful debates and foster critical thinking.
moderationSkills.bullet1: Master the art of neutral facilitation
moderationSkills.bullet2: Learn to ask probing questions that deepen analysis
moderationSkills.bullet3: Practice managing different personality types and viewpoints
moderationSkills.bullet4: Develop timing and pacing for effective discussions

criticalThinking.title: Critical Thinking Through Argument Analysis
criticalThinking.content: Enhance your analytical skills by evaluating AI arguments and developing deeper understanding of reasoning patterns.
criticalThinking.bullet1: Analyze the quality and logic of AI-generated arguments
criticalThinking.bullet2: Identify strengths and weaknesses in reasoning patterns
criticalThinking.bullet4: Recognize bias and perspective in historical accounts

reflection.title: Collaborative Reflection & Self-Assessment 2.0
reflection.content: Engage in meaningful reflection to enhance your moderation skills and track your growth as a facilitator.
reflection.bullet1: Engage in structured reflection with peers and teachers
reflection.bullet2: Analyze moderation effectiveness and learning outcomes
reflection.bullet3: Provide and receive constructive feedback on facilitation skills
reflection.bullet4: Document growth in critical thinking and leadership abilities

applications.title: Educational Benefits Over Human Debates

applications.bullet3: Consistent availability of diverse character perspectives
applications.bullet4: Opportunity for shy students to practice leadership skills

impersonaTu.title: ImpersonaTu Tutorial
impersonaTu.subtitle: The student plays a historical character and debates with another character played by the AI

welcome.title: Welcome to ImpersonaTu!
welcome.content: The student becomes a historical character and discusses a topic with another character played by the artificial intelligence.
welcome.bullet1: The student speaks in the first person, as their character would
welcome.bullet2: The AI answers in the role of the other character
welcome.bullet3: At the end come a reflection and an evaluation

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.content: Three choices are enough to start: who you play, who you talk to and what you discuss.
howItWorks.bullet1: Choose your character and the AI's (they must be different)
howItWorks.bullet2: Write the topic, for example "Is war ever just?"
howItWorks.bullet3: Talk by typing, by dictation or, if enabled, by voice
howItWorks.bullet4: End whenever you want, after the minimum number of turns

inRole.title: Staying in character
inRole.content: The value of the activity is reasoning like the character, not quoting them.
inRole.bullet1: Use the ideas and language of their time
inRole.bullet2: Give reasons: "As Galileo I argue that… because…"
inRole.bullet3: Answer objections without leaving the role

skills.title: What students learn
skills.content: Playing a point of view different from one's own trains historical and critical thinking.
skills.bullet1: Historical empathy: understanding choices made in another context
skills.bullet2: Arguing with evidence and reasons, not just opinions
skills.bullet3: Recognising the limits and biases of every position

reflection.title: Reflection and evaluation
reflection.content: At the end the student writes a short reflection and gets an evaluation from the AI.
reflection.bullet1: The reflection asks what they understood about the character and the topic
reflection.bullet2: The evaluation grades the conversation and the reflection
reflection.bullet3: The teacher sees the full chat and the grades, and can add their own feedback

classroom.title: In the classroom
classroom.content: The teacher can assign the activity with characters, topic and goals already chosen.
classroom.bullet1: History: Caesar and Cicero on the republic
classroom.bullet2: Science: Galileo and Bellarmine on the scientific method
classroom.bullet3: Literature: an author and one of their critics
classroom.bullet4: With assignment goals, JEV signals when the student has reached them

doppiaIntervista.title: Double Interview Tutorial
doppiaIntervista.subtitle: Interview two characters together and compare their answers

welcome.title: Welcome to Double Interview!
welcome.content: The student interviews two characters in the same conversation and compares how they answer the same questions.
welcome.bullet1: Two different characters, played by the AI
welcome.bullet2: Questions can go to both or to just one
welcome.bullet3: Direct comparison brings out different ideas, values and contexts

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.content: Choose two characters and ask your questions: each one answers in their own voice.
howItWorks.bullet1: Choose two characters (they must be different)
howItWorks.bullet2: With "Ask" choose whether the question goes to both or to one
howItWorks.bullet3: Each character only hears the questions addressed to them
howItWorks.bullet4: End whenever you want, after the minimum number of turns

questions.title: Asking good questions
questions.content: The best questions force both characters to take a stand.
questions.bullet1: Ask both the same question to compare the answers
questions.bullet2: Prefer open questions: "Why…?", "What would you have done if…?"
questions.bullet3: Ask one of them to comment on what the other said

comparison.title: Comparing the answers
comparison.content: During the interview and at the end, look for similarities and differences.
comparison.bullet1: What do they agree and disagree on?
comparison.bullet2: How much do their times or cultures matter?
comparison.bullet3: Which arguments are more convincing, and why?

reflection.title: Reflection and evaluation
reflection.content: At the end the student writes a short reflection and gets an evaluation from the AI.
reflection.bullet1: The reflection asks which differences emerged
reflection.bullet2: The evaluation grades the conversation and the reflection
reflection.bullet3: The teacher sees the full chat and the grades, and can add their own feedback

classroom.title: In the classroom
classroom.content: The teacher can assign the activity with the two characters and goals already chosen.
classroom.bullet1: History: Lincoln and Garibaldi on freedom
classroom.bullet2: Philosophy: Plato and Aristotle on knowledge
classroom.bullet3: Science: Newton and Einstein on gravity
classroom.bullet4: With assignment goals, JEV signals when the student has reached them
